Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up and next steps

Hey Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Recap
- Primary use case: real-time personalization + multi-turn chat for patient support; model: Llama-3-13B (open variant) for generation + embeddings for retrieval.
- Estimated steady-state volume: ~25M tokens / month (average).
- Burst profile: occasional spikes during promo windows / clinics onboarding; observed bursts up to ~4M tokens over 10-15 minute windows (~250-400k tokens/min for very short intervals).
- SLA needs: p50 latency target <200ms for token streaming; ability to tolerate short, controlled throttling during extreme spikes.

Pricing / unit economics (from today's discussion)
- Budget guidance you gave: target $/1M tokens between $0.75–$1.25 (you mentioned $1.00 as a target).
- Our baseline public pricing (for context): $1.50 / 1M tokens for this model family on hosted; dedicated/committed tiers can get meaningfully lower unit prices.

Rate limits & overage framing
- Quotas: we provision a monthly token quota tied to the committed plan. For short bursts we can enable temporary quota increases (pre-approved burst buffer) up to X% of baseline for a configurable window.
- Overage: typical approach is to allow overage at a premium multiplier (e.g., 1.25-1.5x the unit price) or to route excess to a lower-cost / higher-latency fallback model to avoid steep charges.
- For ZenHealth specifically I propose:
  1) Committed plan: 24M/month (close to your 25M estimate) with a unit price target of $1.00 / 1M tokens.
  2) Burst buffer: pre-approved short bursts up to +30% of baseline for up to 30 minutes (automatic) at the same committed unit price, with usage above that subject to overage pricing.
  3) Overage: billed at 1.35x the committed unit price (so $1.35 / 1M) for the remainder of the month unless you opt to enable a lower-cost fallback model path.

Questions / next steps (need your confirmation)
- Can you confirm the steady monthly estimate (25M is what we heard)? If the true baseline is higher/lower we'll adjust the committed amount.
- Is the proposed burst buffer (+30% / 30 min) acceptable, or do you need a higher short-term headroom?
- Procurement & security: you mentioned SOC2 + basic audit artifacts. I attached a short rate-limits doc and will pull SOC2 evidence into the folder once I have the procurement contact.

Attachments: redwood-rate-limits.pdf (one-page explainer with sample quota configs)

Proposed next steps
- If you agree, I'll create a Mutual Action Plan and draft the committed pricing line for Rafael to review.
- Suggest a 30-min follow-up Wed or Thu to finalize quota + procurement checklist.

Thanks — Marissa

--

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Monthly baseline: yes, 25M tokens/month is the right ballpark for the next 6 months. Expect growth of ~15% q/q as we roll out to more clinics.

2) Bursts: our busiest events are onboarding waves (new clinic cohorts) where we can see a 10-15 minute spike that totals ~3.5-4M tokens. Outside of those windows, minute-level sustained rates are under 200k tokens/min.

3) Budget: we're aiming for ~$1.00 / 1M tokens on committed spend. Procurement is open to 1.25x overage if it's capped and predictable.

4) Security/procurement: looping in procurement@zenhealth.com (they prefer standard SOC2 + IP/data handling language). Priya is our PM and will help coordinate the MAP.

We're aligned on the approach — two asks:
- Please confirm the exact overage multiplier and whether we can set a hard cap (e.g., stop ingestion beyond +50% of baseline unless explicitly approved).
- Can you attach the draft MAP and a quick pricing table showing committed price vs overage price vs fallback model price?

Alex
VP Product, ZenHealth
alex.chen@zenhealth.com

Overage multiplier & caps
- Proposal: overage billed at 1.35x committed unit price (so $1.35 / 1M) up to a hard cap of +50% of committed monthly quota. Once +50% is reached, we will automatically throttle to a configurable fallback model or pause ingest until a brief approval is received from your procurement contact.
- We can add an explicit "stop ingestion" toggle for procurement to control automated behavior at the cap.

MAP & pricing table
- I created a draft MAP and pricing table and attached it (ZenHealth_MAP.pdf). The MAP includes: committed qty 24M, unit price $1.00 / 1M, burst buffer +30% for 30 minutes, overage price $1.35 / 1M up to +50% cap, optional fallback routing price $0.60 / 1M (lower-cost model).
- Rafael will run the numbers through a quick model to show monthly $ impact at different growth scenarios; Rafael — can you produce a 12-month projection (baseline + 15% q/q) and three header rows: committed spend, expected overage, fallback savings?

Procurement / SOC2
- Procurement — can you confirm the best address for docs? We will add SOC2 + audit artifact links into the shared folder and include a short onboarding checklist for your security team.

Next call
- Proposed times: Wed 11:00am PT or Thu 9:30am PT for a 30-min sync to finalize MAP and procurement checklist. Please confirm.

If that all sounds good I'll convert the MAP to a formal quote and route it for signature (DocuSign link will be provided).
